answer_core:
I would not choose the advisor's hybrid direction yet. Keep the political sequence clean: talk to your advisor first, use Dr. Silva only as a low-cost reality check, and go to the committee only after you know whether the data path is real.

The decision should turn on two gates. First, Silva/data access: within the next two weeks, get dated, concrete evidence that Dr. Silva can provide usable data, that access is allowed, and that the collaboration would be deep enough for dissertation work. Second, fallback viability: confirm with your advisor that the lab's safer path is advisor-backed, resourced, technically ready, identity-coherent for you, and protected by clear stop-loss criteria if it fails to produce dissertation-grade results.

Until both gates pass, treat option 3 as promising but unproven, and treat the fallback as a plan that still has to earn your trust. Do not go around your advisor with a finished proposal. Do not run all three options in parallel. Set dated evidence checks, then choose the path that gives you the best chance of finishing a PhD.
